risks.description: Approval may not be recorded durably.
Approving twice may apply the effect twice.

POST /approve may return 200 'approved' from the in-memory view while never writing the durable store, so a fresh-process re-read still sees pending. This is the exact shape of the wave-1 cluster (durable store did not show status=approved).
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001; wave-1 clusters C01/C03; diff r5/fixture/app.py

risks.description: Approve is not guarded against re-application, so a concurrent or retried approve records more than one payment for a single invoice (wave-1 gen-idempotent saw payments!=1).
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001; wave-1 cluster C02; diff r5/fixture/app.py

risks.description: The approve effect may land but the response stall past the client timeout, leaving the caller unable to tell whether the approval was recorded; only durable state reveals the truth.
An approval that appears immediately after write may not survive a re-read of persisted state once other operations touch the store.

scenarios.title: Two simultaneous approvals of one invoice record a single payment durably
scenarios.purpose: Exercise the race between two approve requests on the same invoice: after both land, the durable store must show exactly one approval and one payment, not two.
scenarios.rationale: The covered idempotency case is two SEQUENTIAL approves. A concurrent pair stresses the in-process lock plus the status guard together, which is the realistic double-pay path. Correct code keeps payments=1/approvals=1; a missing guard yields payments=2/approvals=2; a non-durable write yields pending/payments=0. Durable state (not the 200s) is the oracle.
expected_observations: Durable store shows W2-CONC status=approved with approvals=1 and payments=1
forbidden_observations: Durable store shows payments=2 or approvals=2 (double application under concurrency)
Durable store shows status=pending or payments=0 (approval not persisted)
scenarios.isolation_note: Uses a dedicated invoice id (W2-CONC) never touched by another scenario; writes are keyed per-invoice so they cannot contaminate other scenarios. state.py is read-only. No write-capable cleanup command exists, so isolation relies on the unique id.

scenarios.title: Approval survives a fresh-process re-read after intervening operations
scenarios.purpose: Approve one invoice, then perform other traffic (approve a different invoice, GET the first), then re-read the first invoice's DURABLE state from a fresh process — it must still be approved.
scenarios.rationale: AC-APPROVAL-002 is about surviving a RE-READ, distinct from the covered immediate write check. Reading via state.py is a fresh OS process reading the file, and the intervening approve+GET ensure the value is durable through subsequent activity rather than a transient in-memory reflection. A UI-lies defect surfaces as status=pending on the durable re-read.
expected_observations: After intervening operations, a fresh-process re-read of W2-READ shows status=approved with approvals=1 and payments=1
forbidden_observations: Durable re-read of W2-READ shows status=pending (approval did not survive the re-read)
scenarios.isolation_note: Uses dedicated invoice ids W2-READ and W2-READ-OTHER; per-invoice writes cannot affect other scenarios. state.py is read-only. Deliberately does NOT restart the service (boot reseeds the store), so it tests a fresh-process re-read of the file, which is the fixture's own definition of persisted-state re-read.

scenarios.title: Approval is durably recorded even when the client request times out
scenarios.purpose: Issue an approve with a short client timeout; regardless of whether the response returns, the durable store must reflect exactly one recorded approval — the caller cannot rely on the 200.
scenarios.rationale: The endpoint may apply the effect and then stall past the client timeout. Per the hard rule, an ambiguous-outcome scenario must inspect persisted state: the request may or may not return, but the durable store must show status=approved / payments=1. Correct or effect-lands-then-stalls both pass; a non-durable defect surfaces as pending/payments=0.
expected_observations: Durable store shows W2-TMO status=approved with payments=1, whether or not the HTTP call returned within the timeout
forbidden_observations: Durable store shows status=pending / payments=0 after the approve attempt
scenarios.isolation_note: Dedicated invoice id W2-TMO; per-invoice write. state.py is read-only. A client-side timeout on the request is an EXPECTED, acceptable observation here — the durable state_check, not the HTTP response, is the oracle.

scenarios.title: Retrying an approve after an ambiguous timeout does not double-pay
scenarios.purpose: Model the 3am client behavior: the first approve times out ambiguously, the operator retries the same invoice, and the durable store must still show a single payment.
scenarios.rationale: Distinct from the covered two-clean-approves idempotency case: here the first call is ambiguous (short timeout), then the client retries. This is the realistic retry path that must remain safe. Correct/effect-then-stall keeps payments=1 across the retry; an unguarded approve records payments=2; a non-durable defect shows pending. Durable state is the oracle, since the caller could not confirm the first attempt.
expected_observations: After an ambiguous first attempt and a retry, durable store shows W2-RTY status=approved with approvals=1 and payments=1
forbidden_observations: Durable store shows payments=2 or more (retry double-paid)
Durable store shows status=pending (approval never persisted)
scenarios.isolation_note: Dedicated invoice id W2-RTY; per-invoice write. state.py read-only. First request may time out client-side (acceptable); durable state after the retry is the oracle.

assumptions: The 'api' service serves the approval endpoint at http://127.0.0.1:8952 and writes to the same store.json that `python3 r5/fixture/state.py` reads, so state.py is a valid durable oracle for it.
`python3 r5/fixture/state.py <invoice_id>` prints a single line '<id> status=... approvals=N payments=N' filtered to that id, and prints nothing for an unknown id.
Approving an unknown invoice id auto-creates it, so each scenario can safely use a unique id (W2-CONC, W2-READ, W2-TMO, W2-RTY) to stay isolated.
No write-capable command is on the approved list, so cleanup is impossible; isolation relies entirely on per-scenario unique invoice ids plus the read-only nature of state.py.
A client-side request timeout is treated as an acceptable, expected observation in the ambiguous-outcome scenarios; the durable state_check is the authoritative pass/fail signal there.
unresolved_questions: AC-APPROVAL-002 says approval state must 'survive a re-read of persisted state', but the service reseeds/clears store.json on every boot (app.py main() unlinks and reseeds). Does 'survives a re-read' include surviving a full service restart, or only a fresh-process read of the store file? A restart-recovery test would fail even for correct code under the current boot logic, so I did not author one — the intended durability boundary needs confirmation.

Should an approval require an authenticated/valid actor? The endpoint accepts a missing or malformed body and records actor='unknown'. The ACs do not promise actor attribution or input validation, so I did not invent a scenario for it.
Is auto-creating an invoice on first approve of an unknown id intended behavior, or should approving a non-existent invoice be rejected? The ACs are silent on invoice existence.
